what: What did each Lunenburg town employee earn in 1969?
why: `report-gross-wages` holds per-employee earnings from the 1995-2010 reports and FY2011-FY2025. The 1969 annual town report prints no wage list: the whole text (132 pages) was searched for wage, gross, salary and payroll and found only aggregates (the accountant's wage lines in the schedule, p33-35 and p39, `Payroll Deductions` p20, p30), prose about salaries (p16, p52, p60, p89, p91), the Personnel Board's proposed schedule (p17) and the School Personnel Listing (p107-116), which names staff, education and years of experience and prints no pay (sources/data/report-tables/1969/). — closes: the Town's calendar-1969 payroll register (W-2 totals by employee) from the Treasurer's office.

what: What were the town's non-union salary grades and step rates as voted in 1969?
why: `salary-schedule` and `report-classification-plan` read Schedule A from the 2010 report and FY2011 onward. The 1969 report prints the Personnel Board's PROPOSED schedule for the March 7, 1970 meeting (p17, landed as `report-proposed-salary-schedule`) and the vote on the schedule `dated March 1, 1969` (Article 4, p65, which refers to page 11 of the 1968 Annual Report) but not that schedule's rates; searched for classification, salary schedule, grade and step (sources/data/report-tables/1969/). — closes: the Personnel Board's Classification and Salary Schedule dated March 1, 1969 (page 11 of the 1968 Annual Report).

what: What did each special revenue fund take in, spend and carry forward in 1969, town-wide?
why: `special-revenue-funds` holds forward, receipts, disbursements and balance by fund from the 1995-2010 reports. The 1969 report prints the revolving funds' YEAR-END balances only, as lines of the balance sheet (p20 `Revolving Funds`: School Lunch 3,723.19, School Athletics 107.02), the school lunch and athletic accounts inside the School Department's own reports (p118, p125) and revenue lines in the Treasurer's receipts (p26); no town-wide receipts-and-disbursements schedule by fund. Searched revolving and special revenue: the only hit is p20 (sources/data/report-tables/1969/). — closes: the Town Accountant's calendar-1969 special revenue fund ledger.

what: What was appropriated, spent and carried forward on each capital project fund in 1969?
why: `report-capital-projects` holds a separate capital project fund schedule from the 2001-2010 reports. The 1969 report prints no such schedule: the accountant's schedule lists each special article with its balance (p31-42), the balance sheet carries the unexpended appropriation balances (p21), the Middle School and Jr.-Sr. High School appear as bonds (p43), and no capital plan is printed; so whether any project sat in a separate fund is not shown. Searched capital project, capital plan and capital improvement: the only hits are p85 (the Montachusett Regional Vocational School District's own `Capital Budget of $239,620.00`, debt service and retirement, a different government) and p122 (`ASSETS (Capital Outlay)`, a School Department budget series), neither a Town fund (sources/data/report-tables/1969/). — closes: the Town Accountant's calendar-1969 capital projects fund ledger.

what: What was Lunenburg's assessed valuation by property class, its levy, overlay and new growth for 1969?
why: `report-valuation` holds the valuation and levy history from the 1987-2010 reports. The 1969 report prints the assessed valuation as two lines of the opening facts page (p3: real estate $12,036,520, personal property $1,195,130, tax rate $133.00, no year printed beside any of them), and prose that 1969 was the town's `Year of Revaluation` (p9), and no recapitulation of the levy, the overlay or growth. The overlay appears only as a reserve and a funding source (p20, p66). Searched valuation, overlay, tax rate, levy and growth (sources/data/report-tables/1969/). — closes: the Assessors' 1969 tax rate recapitulation (the Tax Recap sheet filed with the State).

what: How many weighing and measuring devices did the Sealer test in 1969, and what did sealing bring in by device?
why: `report-weights-measures` holds the Sealer's device counts and `sealing-fee-schedule` the fee per device from the 2001-2010 reports. The 1969 report gives the year's counts in prose on p59 (24 scales and 43 weights inspected, 1 scale condemned, 51 gasoline pumps inspected and 35 re-inspected) and the Treasurer's receipts one line, `Inspector of Weights and Measures` $283.50 (p25), with no fee by device type. Searched weights and measures, sealer, sealing (sources/data/report-tables/1969/). — closes: the Inspector of Weights and Measures' 1969 test and fee record.
